title: Endpoint QuickSwitch: Dynamic fallback & progressive rollout playbook for chat/completions/embeddings/rerank
creator: Ava Martinez
description: This PRD defines the Endpoint QuickSwitch feature: a unified playbook and API-level behavior to perform progressive rollouts and automated dynamic fallbacks for Hosted inference endpoints (chat, completions, embeddings, rerank). QuickSwitch enables traffic splits, automated model-variant fallback on degradation, and an operator-friendly rollback path while preserving deterministic routing and observability metadata.
background: Customers running production LLM features require predictable SLAs during model rollouts and incident recovery. Current manual rollback patterns are slow and error-prone: operators swap endpoints or change routing outside the API and lose fine-grained attribution and metrics. QuickSwitch bundles a controlled rollout mechanism with built-in degradation detection and automatic fallback to a compatible model variant (e.g., quantized path or previous checkpoint) to preserve availability and avoid customer-visible errors.
scope_in_scope: API surface: /endpoints.rollout.apply and rollout metadata returned on inference responses
Traffic split config per endpoint: percentages, model_variant tags, region overrides
Automatic fallback policies: latency/SLO/quality triggers mapped to a target model variant
Per-request fallback reason codes surfaced in response headers and Console traces
Console experience: rollout creation UI, traffic visualization, and single-click abort/rollback
Integration with existing routing policies and cost-aware routing (use cheaper variant when light degradation detected)
Acceptance tests + canary validation harness for chat/completions/embeddings/rerank
scope_out_of_scope: New training/finetuning flows or model publishing mechanics
Autoscaling primitives for Dedicated pools (engineering will consume rollout signals but autoscaling changes are separate)
requirements: R1: API must accept a rollout request that specifies: endpoint_id, ordered list of model_variants with weights, rollout_duration, health_checks (latency P95 threshold, error-rate threshold, quality regression threshold), and fallback_policy mapping
R2: Runtime must enforce per-request deterministic routing based on active rollout weights and honor region and capacity overrides
R3: Runtime must monitor configured health_checks and trigger automated fallback if thresholds breached for N consecutive windows (configurable, default 3 windows of 1 minute)
R4: When fallback occurs, response must include a standardized header 'x-quick-fallback: <variant_id>;reason=<code>' and Console trace link
R5: Console must show live traffic split, a simple graph of health_check metrics, and allow operator-initiated step-up/abort/rollback
R6: Rollout operations must be auditable and logged (actor, timestamp, config diff) and visible in endpoint activity stream
R7: SDKs (python/js) must expose start_rollout and get_rollout_status helpers and map to the REST contract
R8: Quality signal integration: accept boolean pass/fail from offline eval sets and permit gating rollouts on eval pass
R9: Rollback must support three modes: immediate full rollback, gradual reverse rollout, and pause (freeze weights)
acceptance_criteria: AC1: Create a rollout targeting a test endpoint (chat) to split 10% v2 / 90% v1 over 24 hours; system adheres to configured weights within +/-2% measured at 5 minute granularity

AC2: Configure a health_check with latency P95 > 400ms threshold; when runtime observes sustained regression per policy, requests are routed to fallback variant and 'x-quick-fallback' header is present on >=99% of affected requests
AC3: Console shows rollout timeline, weights, and an operator can abort and fully rollback to v1 within 15 seconds of action (UI + API path verified)
AC4: SDK helpers return rollout status with same canonical fields as REST and tests exist for python/js packages

AC5: No error-rate or quality regressions outside baseline: during a staged rollout to 20% traffic, end-to-end request success rate must not drop below 99.0% for chat/completions/embeddings/rerank compared to a control period
AC6: Audit logs contain rollout creator, timestamp, exact config diff, and any automated fallback events with reason codes for at least 90 days
AC7: Performance guardrails: enabling QuickSwitch should not add more than 10ms median latency overhead in the runtime path for steady-state requests
AC8: End-to-end e2e test runs in CI validate fallback trigger behavior using a synthetic latency injector and a synthetic quality regression harness

rollout_plan: Phase 1 (Internal staging): enable QuickSwitch for internal endpoints only; validate traffic weighting, fallback behavior, and Console UI. Phase 2 (Customer beta): 5 invited customers; monitor daily for 2 weeks; collect qualitative feedback. Phase 3 (Gradual GA): open to all customers behind feature flag; region-by-region enablement with capacity gating and 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 50% -> 100% cadence, with minimum 24h observation windows between steps unless manual override. Abort thresholds: latency P95 > configured threshold or error-rate spike > 2x baseline for 3 consecutive windows triggers automatic rollback.
metrics_and_slo: M1: Rollout-weight accuracy: measured traffic share vs target within +/-2% at 5 minute resolution
M2: Fallback accuracy: when fallback triggered, >=99% of affected requests include fallback header
M3: Latency impact: median added latency < 10ms; P95 increase < 30ms
M4: Availability: endpoint success rate >= 99.9% during rollouts (customer-facing SLO enforcement), or no customer-facing errors due to rollout
M5: Cost delta: report per-token cost delta for fallback events and for active variant splits (show in Console)
open_risks: RISK-1: False-positive fallback due to noisy telemetry might cause unnecessary rollbacks - mitigation: multi-window aggregation + manual override
RISK-2: Edge case when client pins to a specific variant via custom routing header will bypass QuickSwitch; we need clear docs and an SDK pragma to respect rollout policies
RISK-3: Interaction with Dedicated reserved capacity: some variants might be in different capacity tiers; the routing layer must account for capacity lead times
RISK-4: Quality gating for embeddings and rerank requires representative evals; poor eval sets can block rollouts unnecessarily
notes: Design trade-offs discussed: we opted for runtime-internal routing rather than client-side split to preserve metrics and observability. This increases runtime complexity but keeps attribution correct.
We chose header-based fallback signaling for minimal SDK changes and so that customers can immediately detect fallbacks in logs.
Plan includes a phased developer-first SDK rollout to avoid breaking customers who read raw response bodies. Backwards compatibility tests included.
